title: Pontiac Firebird Engines by Year (1967–2002)
description: Every factory engine in the Pontiac Firebird and Trans Am by year, 1967–2002: OHC six, Ram Air and Super Duty 455, 301 Turbo, TPI, LT1 and LS1.
intro: Pontiac built the Firebird from 1967 to 2002 alongside the Camaro. Until 1976 it used Pontiac's own engines. From 1977 many came from Chevrolet, Buick and Oldsmobile, and the notes say which division built each one.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: First generation
intro: Pontiac's version of the Camaro started with an overhead-cam inline six that no other American maker offered. The V8s ran from the 326 (350 from 1968) up to the 400, which went through three Ram Air versions by 1969.

generations.name: Second generation
intro: The second generation went from the 1970 Ram Air IV to the 1973–1974 Super Duty 455 and, from 1977, a mix of Pontiac, Oldsmobile, Chevrolet and Buick engines. The 1980–1981 Turbo Trans Am used a turbocharged 301.

generations.name: Third generation
intro: The third generation offered the Iron Duke four, Chevrolet V6s and 305 and 350 V8s, with Tuned Port Injection from 1985, and the 1989 Turbo Trans Am's 3.8 turbo V6.

generations.name: Fourth generation
intro: The fourth generation used the LT1 350 until 1997 and the aluminum LS1 from 1998, with WS6 Ram Air versions, plus Chevrolet and Buick V6s. SLP Firehawk conversions were dealer-installed and are not listed.
